body.estimand_functional: The causal estimand remains \(\tau_n=E_{P_n}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=1]\), and \(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}\) is a sample-selected estimator aimed at that estimand, not a definition of it.  The current core does not establish an unconditional weak law for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\).  The proved conditional transfer lemma yields the displayed Gaussian-quadratic coordinate only after its joint Gaussian coupling and quantitative near-minimizer condition have independently been established.  The boundary-obstruction theorem proves that the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process, and any covariance-only Gaussian repair, cannot provide that coupling on the present regular class because a first-order fixed-cardinality boundary term may be non-Gaussian.  It does not prove that the selected marginal law fails; identifying the rank-boundary-corrected process and selected law is the formal open question.

sampling_model.design: Fixed-stratum superpopulation triangular arrays contain exactly \(n_{\mathcal R}\) randomized-trial records and \(n_{\mathcal E}\) external-control records; \(P_n\) is only the deterministic-fraction reference mixture.
sampling_model.units: Within each row the two strata are mutually independent, observations are independent within strata, and both deterministic stratum fractions stay bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is randomized only in the fixed trial stratum; every record in the fixed external stratum is observed under control and carries the observed tie breaker \(V\).
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment and reference-mixture trial-source propensities are uniformly bounded away from zero on the trial covariate support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A prespecified fold map selects learners whose existence and \(L_2\) rate are properties of the nuisance tuple; the displayed estimator evaluates those learners out of fold, while the anchor influence ranking is the exact full-trial empirical functional.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~2 gives \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) MSE estimation for any given borrowed set, and Theorem~3 gives selection consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive separation.
Theorem~1 gives asymptotic normality of a fixed-prefix estimator after centering by its prefix-specific bias.
Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

body.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated fixed-cardinality ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion.  Two counterexamples now lie inside the displayed Yang--Li--Wu--Yang sample maps: both use the genuine squared outcome-regression loss and an empirically fitted influence score whose continuous ordering is preserved with probability tending to one.  The first shows that the frozen fixed-threshold influence process omits a first-order empirical rank-boundary term that can be non-Gaussian, so its all-prefix Gaussian coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail.  The second gives exactly equal leading MSE at the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes while their root-\(n\) ATE coordinates stay separated, so \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\) without relying on the no-borrowing candidate or the auxiliary tie breaker.  The selected law, sharp excess modulus, and computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.

project_justification.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's equation~(2) fits a squared outcome-regression loss, equation~(3) ranks individual external controls by the generated influence score, Algorithm~1 forms positive top-\(k\) prefixes, Theorem~1 treats a given borrowed set, Theorem~2 estimates its MSE pointwise, and Theorem~3 assumes a given ranking and a fixed positive MSE gap.  None supplies the rank-boundary-corrected all-prefix expansion, the local-gap selected law, or post-selection ATE coverage at multiple minima.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a selector-specific modulus separating prefixes that are close in leading MSE from prefixes that are close as root-\(n\) ATE coordinates.  The anchor-exact positive-prefix witness shows that the unrestricted regular class has a positive exact-tie cost even when the empirical score ordering is continuous and stable; useful adaptation therefore requires additional observable localization beyond a score-density margin.
project_justification.fill: The project proves on an anchor-exact regular subclass that the frozen-covariance all-prefix extension is non-representative, proves on a second anchor-exact regular subclass that two positive top-\(k\) candidates can have identical leading risk and separated ATE coordinates, retains the earlier finite-support calculation as an independent algebraic witness, and isolates a rigorous conditional stability transfer lemma.  It does not claim an unconditional law for the generated selector.  The remaining problem is to derive the rank-boundary-corrected estimator and criterion process, together with primitive near-minimizer control, before constructing tie-uniform inference.

body.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the squared outcome-regression empirical risk minimizer in equation~(2), its generated influence score in equation~(3), and the nested positive top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1.  Their Theorem~1 gives bias-centered Gaussian behavior for a given borrowed set, Theorem~2 gives pointwise MSE estimation for any given set, and Theorem~3 gives consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive MSE separation.  The present witnesses use those same squared-loss and generated-ranking maps, embedded in fixed-stratum local triangular arrays: one shows that the empirical fixed-cardinality boundary can contribute a non-Gaussian first-order term omitted by the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process, and another gives an exact leading-risk tie between the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes with nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance.  These results do not contradict the anchor's fixed-set theorems; they block an unproved uniform local-gap extension of them.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess study focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, not generated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher give the generic local nonuniformity background.  Fang and Santos motivate derivative-aware resampling at nondifferentiable maps.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo derive sorting derivatives under stronger score-index regularity, while Chernozhukov and coauthors provide orthogonal fixed-target expansions and high-dimensional Gaussian or multiplier approximations only after the correct ranked functional has been derived.  The localization architectures of Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey become applicable only after that process is identified.  Zhu, Yang, and Wang study sharp-null randomization validity and conformal threshold borrowing rather than weak-null superpopulation ATE inference for this selector.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The negative bridge is exact for the anchor's displayed squared-loss influence ranking but uses deliberately misspecified intercept outcome regressions and disconnected trial covariate support.  The boundary witness also lets the trial--external mean discrepancy oscillate at the empirical quantile scale; a score-density margin alone does not rule this out.  The positive-prefix tie witness is smoother and remains in the regular class, but it establishes only a positive exact-tie modulus.  A positive selected-law theorem still requires primitive linearization of the external empirical-quantile boundary and the trial-generated score perturbation, plus score-index smoothness or another condition controlling conditional contributions and quantitative stability of random near minimizers.
body.honest_scope: The proved negative results remain logically separate.  On one anchor-exact regular sequence, a deterministic interior generated prefix has a non-Gaussian rank-boundary contribution, invalidating the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian coupling and any covariance-only Gaussian repair.  On a second anchor-exact regular sequence, the positive one-quarter and one-half prefixes have exactly equal leading MSE but asymptotically separated ATE coordinates; the independent finite-support theorem supplies an additional no-borrowing witness.  None proves that the generated MSE selector chooses the non-Gaussian coordinate, so no selected marginal law has been established or refuted.  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma is not an achievability theorem for the generated path.  The rank-boundary-corrected local-gap process, the sharp excess modulus, and a computable uniformly valid multiplier interval remain formal open questions.
